rows.title: Remembering Allan McDonald: He Refused To Approve Challenger Launch, Exposed Cover-Up
rows.standfirst: Allan McDonald, who directed the booster rocket project at NASA contractor Morton Thiokol, urged delaying the launch of the space shuttle before it exploded in 1986. He has died at age 83.

rows.title: 'We're Here, We Deserve Dignity': Arab Americans Advocate For Little Arabia In Calif.
rows.standfirst: Members of the community in Anaheim have been advocating for an official designation of the vibrant district for more than a decade. But the city council has been reluctant to support the efforts.

rows.title: 'Why Us?': A Year After Being Laid Off, Millions Are Still Unemployed
rows.standfirst: Millions who lost jobs at the beginning of the pandemic are still out of the labor force, making up levels of the unemployed not seen since the Great Recession.

rows.title: Far-Right Misinformation Is Thriving On Facebook. A New Study Shows Just How Much
rows.standfirst: Research from New York University found that far-right accounts known for spreading misinformation drive engagement at higher rates than other news sources.

rows.title: Senate Passes $1.9 Trillion Coronavirus Relief Package
rows.standfirst: The package would deliver a new round of financial assistance to Americans grappling with the impact of the pandemic. The House will need to vote on the final version.

rows.title: Hold That Drill: Why Wall Street Wants Energy Companies To Pump Less Oil, Not More
rows.standfirst: After bankrolling oil companies for years and seeing poor returns, investors are now pressuring companies to keep their oil output lower, instead of higher.

rows.title: 'It Really Is A Gag Order': California May Limit Nondisclosure Agreements
rows.standfirst: Former Pinterest employee Ifeoma Ozoma risked a lawsuit when she made public her allegations of workplace discrimination and harassment. She hopes California will ban contracts like the one she had.

rows.title: California Set To Open Ballparks, Arenas And Theme Parks In April
rows.standfirst: Attendance for sporting events, live music and theme parks will vary at the county level based on COVID-19 infection rates. Only in-state residents will be allowed to attend.

rows.title: Jobs Friday: Better! Still Not Good Tho
rows.standfirst: It's Jobs Friday! The February jobs report shows signs of recovery, but there's still a long way to go. We talk to three experts about their indicators on how things will change and when.

rows.title: The Marriage Pact
rows.standfirst: They say true love is hard to find. Whoever says that isn't an economist. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: What's An NFT? And Why Are People Paying Millions To Buy Them?
rows.standfirst: The latest Internet hype is about a thing that doesn't really exist. Some collectors are spending millions of dollars on these digital items called nonfungible tokens, or NFTs.

rows.title: 'Tragic': Driving Was Down In 2020, But Traffic Fatality Rates Surged
rows.standfirst: A report estimates that traffic deaths rose 8% last year compared to 2019. When measured by number of miles driven, fatalities surged by 24%, the highest in nearly a century.

rows.title: Senate Democrats Cut Back Planned Unemployment Benefits Extension
rows.standfirst: The change is a compromise between progressive members who wanted enhanced benefits for several more months and moderate Democrats who wanted to curb the weekly payments.

rows.title: A Sign Of Hope After 'Winter Hibernation': Employers Add 379,000 Jobs
rows.standfirst: Meanwhile, the unemployment rate dipped to 6.2% last month as the winter wave of coronavirus infections eased.

rows.title: ERCOT CEO Refuses $800K Payout Following Firing
rows.standfirst: The Electric Reliability Council of Texas CEO Bill Magness was removed from his post Wednesday. He informed the organization he will not accept his $800,000 severance.

rows.title: More U.S. Travelers Are Flying Again Despite COVID-19 Risks
rows.standfirst: Friday marked the busiest day for the nation's airports since COVID-19 put the brakes on air travel almost a year ago. But the number of travelers remains far below 2019 levels.

rows.title: France And Germany Pause Use Of AstraZeneca's COVID-19 Vaccine
rows.standfirst: The two countries joined a number of other European nations that have temporarily suspended the shot after several people reportedly developed blood clots after receiving it.

rows.title: Why America Is Moving: Money, Space, Family, Lifestyle ...
rows.standfirst: 2020 made moving a reality for millions. Some moved to be near family. Others achieved their pipe dreams of moving to distant locations in pursuit of a better lifestyle and cheaper cost of living.

rows.title: 'Life-Changing' Stimulus Checks Begin Rolling Out
rows.standfirst: Within days of President Biden signing the relief bill into law, many Americans have been delighted to see bank accounts showing $1,400 deposits already pending.

rows.title: Black Farmers Have Long Faced Discrimination. New Aid Aims To Right Past Wrongs
rows.standfirst: Generations of systemic discrimination have decimated the number of Black farmers in the U.S. Agriculture Secretary Tom Vilsack talked with NPR about new funding for debt relief.

rows.title: Facing Housing Crunch, California Cities Rethink Single-Family Neighborhoods
rows.standfirst: By allowing multi-family housing, proponents across the state say the move could lower housing costs and redress decades of racial segregation.

rows.title: Defense Production Act Speeds Up Vaccine Production
rows.standfirst: A 1950 law allows the government to award contracts that take priority over all others for national defense. During the pandemic, the law has been used to defend the country against the coronavirus.

rows.title: Coronavirus Relief Bill Is A 'Heavy Lift' For Already-Strained IRS
rows.standfirst: The Internal Revenue Service, which has seen budget and staff cuts in recent years, is responsible for carrying out several key provisions of the legislation signed by President Biden this week.

rows.title: How Biden's Plan Could Help Reshape The Finances Of American Families
rows.standfirst: The $1.9 trillion relief bill includes a new monthly allowance for American parents that could help provide a critical lifeline.

rows.title: The $69 Million JPEG
rows.standfirst: An artist called Beeple just sold a piece at Christie's for millions. But it wasn't a painting... it was a kind of crypto. We speak with him and the others behind the first NFT auction. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Relief Act Means 'A Good Night's Sleep' For Food Industry, Says NYC Restaurateur
rows.standfirst: Chef Amanda Cohen, owner of Dirt Candy in New York City, says the coronavirus relief package's $28.6 billion for independent and small-chain restaurants means many in the industry can stay afloat.

rows.title: Chips, Cars and the Baby Bust
rows.standfirst: The Covid-19 pandemic has caused demand shifts and supply chain snafus that have led to many shortages. For Indicators of the Week, we'll be looking at two more: cars and ... babies?

rows.title: High Stakes At A Warehouse: Amazon Fights Against Alabama Union Drive
rows.standfirst: A vote by workers on whether to form Amazon's first unionized warehouse in the U.S. has the community, labor groups and the company on the edge of their seats.

rows.title: Will Posting Memes Or Pro Wedding Pics Land You In Copyright Small Claims Court?
rows.standfirst: Jeff Sedlik's Miles Davis portrait shows up all over the Internet, rarely with his permission, and there's not much he can do to protect himself. Enter the CASE Act, which sounds dull ... but isn't.

rows.title: Manhattan DA Cyrus Vance Jr., Who Is Investigating Trump, Won't Seek Reelection
rows.standfirst: Last month, Vance's office received the former president's tax returns after a years-long battle, after the Supreme Court paved the way for a New York grand jury to obtain and review the documents.

rows.title: Saudi Oil Giant Aramco Reports 44% Profit Slump In 2020 Amid Coronavirus Pandemic
rows.standfirst: Saudi Arabia's state-backed oil company earned $49 billion last year as the pandemic slashed fuel demand around the globe, in what its CEO called "one of the most challenging years in history."

rows.title: After A Year Of Mostly Cancellations, Bookings Are Back For Many Event Venues
rows.standfirst: Phones are once again ringing at event spaces that were largely closed during the pandemic. And venues are starting to navigate the new normal as people being to plan long-postponed celebrations.

rows.title: So How Should Your Favorite Restaurant Pay Its Servers? Well, It's Complicated
rows.standfirst: A fierce debate is taking shape within the restaurant industry as a push to raise the minimum wage threatens to upend the tipped wage structures for servers.

rows.title: CDC Likely To Extend Eviction Moratorium With Millions Of People Behind On Rent
rows.standfirst: The Center for Disease Control and Prevention is moving to extend an order aimed at preventing evictions during the pandemic. Housing groups say the order could prevent up to 1 million evictions.

rows.title: The New Shape Of Pasta
rows.standfirst: What do you do when you can't find the perfect pasta shape? You invent a new shape. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Indicators of the Week! Interest Rates and Global Poverty
rows.standfirst: On the show, we look back at the number of people globally who fell into poverty last year due to the Covid-19 pandemic, and look forward to where U.S. interest rates are projected to stay until 2023.

rows.title: Are We Ready For The Next One? The Striking Pandemic Warnings That Were Ignored
rows.standfirst: Dante Disparte, founder and chairman of Risk Cooperative and member of FEMA's National Advisory Council, explains how lessons from last year can help us in the next pandemic — and why warnings from former Presidents Bush and Obama were not enough to prepare the U.S. for the coronavirus.

rows.title: New $113 Billion NFL Media Rights Deal Gives Fans More Options To Watch Games
rows.standfirst: The NFL has signed new long-term broadcast rights agreements with multiple media partners valued at more than $110 billion over 11 years. The new agreements will start with the 2023 season.

rows.title: Why SkySilk Came Out of Nowhere To Save Parler After Capitol Riot
rows.standfirst: After Amazon took Parler down over violent messages on the site, no tech services firm would help it come back online. Then an obscure Los Angeles-based company offered to help.

rows.title: A Pandemic Winner: How Zoom Beat Tech Giants To Dominate Video Chat
rows.standfirst: Technology let us see and be with each other even when we couldn't do it in person. How did a Silicon Valley upstart beat out the tech powerhouses in video conferencing?

rows.title: The Giant Pool Of Unmatched Music Royalties
rows.standfirst: The music industry has boomed thanks to streaming, but with thousands of new songs being added to platforms everyday, sometimes royalties slip through the cracks unpaid. $424 million worth of royalties, to be exact.

rows.title: Before March Madness, College Athletes Declare They Are #NotNCAAProperty
rows.standfirst: "Players ISOLATED entire year to help make this tournament happen," tweeted Rutgers senior Geo Baker. "NCAA: rewarded w/ $900 million. Players: rewarded w/ free deodorant and small boxed meals."

rows.title: The World's Largest Vaccine Maker Took A Multimillion Dollar Pandemic Gamble
rows.standfirst: NPR tours the factory of the world's largest vaccine maker: Serum Institute of India. It's manufacturing nearly 100 million doses a month of the Oxford-AstraZeneca formula and exporting them globally.

rows.title: A Culinary Tour Of Brexit
rows.standfirst: What has trade with the EU been like for Britons post-Brexit? We answer that question by looking at some of the tastiest indicators around.

rows.title: IRS Postpones Tax Filing Deadline To May 17
rows.standfirst: It is the second consecutive year the agency has given taxpayers more time to file their returns because of the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Johnson & Johnson Reports Vaccine Batch Ruined At Baltimore Factory
rows.standfirst: The drugmaker didn't say how many doses were lost, and it wasn't clear how the problem would impact future deliveries.

rows.title: The Virtual Office
rows.standfirst: The Indicator team has been working remotely for about a year now. While remote work has its perks, sometimes we miss sharing an office space. Can virtual reality help bridge the gap?

rows.title: The Curse Of The Black Lotus (Update)
rows.standfirst: When the popular card game Magic: The Gathering entered a speculative bubble, its creators found a way to keep it from bursting. We check in to see if their strategy is still working. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Journalist Investigates Amazon Warehouse Life And The Pitfalls Of 'One-Click America'
rows.standfirst: Alec MacGillis, author of the new book Fulfillment, says a union vote by Amazon workers in Alabama could determine "what life is going to look like for the working class in America in years to come."

rows.title: N.Y. Gov. Cuomo Signs Marijuana Legalization
rows.standfirst: Critics say in many states the legal marijuana boom hasn't benefited people of color. Lawmakers in New York say their approach avoids those mistakes.

rows.title: 15 Million N95s Without A Buyer
rows.standfirst: The start of the COVID-19 pandemic led to an N95 mask shortage. Now there's still a shortage, but many American mask manufacturers can't sell their masks. We break down the reasons why.

rows.title: Fox Corp. CEO Lachlan Murdoch Heads To Australia As Fox News Faces Headwinds
rows.standfirst: Lachlan Murdoch, the CEO and executive chairman of Fox Corp., has left Los Angeles for Sydney at a time when Fox News is reckoning with major lawsuits and questions over its direction.

rows.title: Volkswagen Will Not Change Its Name To 'Voltswagen' After All, Says It Was All A Joke
rows.standfirst: Volkswagen of America will not, in fact, be renaming itself "Voltswagen of America." A statement to that effect was a joke "in the spirit of April Fool's Day," the company said.

rows.title: Remote Work Is Leading To More Gender And Racial Harassment, Say Tech Workers
rows.standfirst: Women and people of color are reporting the biggest increases in harassment while working remotely during the pandemic, a survey says.

rows.title: What Unemployment Insurance Tells Us About Work During A Pandemic
rows.standfirst: A new study looks at the effect of unemployment benefit generosity on employment levels during the Covid-19 pandemic.

rows.title: 'Fiasco Waiting To Happen': Millions At Risk Of Losing Power Over Unpaid Bills
rows.standfirst: Unpaid electric bills ballooned during the pandemic to more than $27 billion, and many now face the risk of having their power shut off.

rows.title: Evicted And Homeless Due To Pandemic — 'I Literally Had To Sleep In My Car'
rows.standfirst: Getting evicted during COVID can risk a person's health and doom their ability to find a home. The extension this week of a federal order preventing evictions could save many people from that fate.

rows.title: Schmoozing And The Gender Gap
rows.standfirst: Women now make up nearly half of entry level work workers, but there's still a gap higher up on the corporate ladder. One possibility for why this is happening? Schmoozing.

rows.title: Ship Happens: Coffee, Livestock, Ikea Furniture Among The Objects Stuck At The Suez
rows.standfirst: Livestock and lumber. Oil and automobiles. Exercise equipment and instant coffee. These are just some of the products that were blocked by the ship that was stuck in the Suez Canal.

rows.title: Federal Eviction Moratorium Extended Just 2 Days Before Expiration
rows.standfirst: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is extending an order preventing evictions. It was set to expire this week, which could have displaced staggering numbers of people from their homes.
